body: This code doesn't do anything with the URL is something missing from your example?
What version of CakePHP are you using?

Okay, I pulled the code at home tonight and `$this->Auth->redirectUrl(['controller' => 'volunteers', 'action' => 'index']);` worked as expected, so I did a little more digging. The only difference between the two machines and their XAMPP stacks is that at home the Apache DocumentRoot was set to the app's folder while at work the DocumentRoot was set to the app's parent folder. I changed my home DocumentRoot to point to my app's parent folder and sure enough, I was able to duplicate the error.

How can I fix this path problem for an app that is not DocumentRoot?
Knowing that the app has to be in a subdirectory is helpful. I can try to reproduce from that.

> If I replace the array with a string in the call $this->Auth->redirectUrl('volunteers/index'); I receive this error

Your URL needs to start with `/`.

> while at work the DocumentRoot was set to the app's parent folder.

So basically the app is in a subfolder of document root. In that case isn't having the folder name in url expected @markstory ?
Starting the URL with a `/` works when passing a string. How about when passing an array?

issue.body:
When using:
return $this->redirect($this->Auth->redirectUrl());

Instead of redirecting from:
http://localhost/cake3/users/login
to
http://localhost/cake3/articles/

it redirects to:
http://localhost/cake3/cake3/articles/

This does not seem to happen with normal redirect requests and only with auth redirects.
Auth creates /cake3/articles instead of /articles.

( I am running a freshly installed unmodified latest version of Mamp with php 5.5 and have not made any changes to the routing )

body: @ADmad yes, the app being in a subdirectory of documentroot would require the folder name to be present in the url. I think the extra base on the url from redirectUrl() was the problem here.
@markstory Yup I found the issue and fixed it in #3846.
